Junk King Review: Is It Better Than 1-800-GOT-JUNK?

If you’ve ever stared at a pile of unwanted stuff and wondered who could haul it away without breaking the bank, you’ve probably searched “Junk King vs 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK?” The good news? Both companies promise fast, friendly service, but they differ in pricing, coverage, and eco‑friendly policies. In this review we’ll break down the details so you can decide which service fits your budget and values.

Quick Takeaways

  • Pricing: Junk King typically charges by volume, while 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? offers a flat‑rate estimate that’s often higher for smaller loads.
  • Service Area: 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? boasts nationwide coverage; Junk King is strong in the Midwest and South but is expanding eastward.
  • Eco‑Friendly Efforts: Both companies recycle, but 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? has a longer‑standing partnership with local charities.
  • Customer Experience: 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? consistently scores higher on Google Reviews, though Junk King’s “no‑price‑surprise” model wins fans.

Understanding Junk King

What Junk King Promises

Junk King markets itself as a “no‑hassle” junk removal service. The core promise is simple: you call, they show up, you point to what you want gone, and they haul it away. There are no hidden fees for stairs, heavy items, or distance—everything is bundled into the volume‑based price.

How Pricing Works

Junk King measures the load in cubic yards (typically 1‑3 yards). Prices start around $99 for a single‑yard load and increase with each additional yard. This can be a bargain for larger jobs—think whole‑house cleanouts or construction debris—because the per‑yard cost drops as the load grows.

Service Coverage

Junk King operates in 45 U.S. states, with a strong presence in Texas, Ohio, and the Carolinas. If you’re outside their core market, you may still get service, but response times could be longer and pricing may include a travel surcharge.

Eco‑Friendly Initiatives

Junk King claims that up to 80% of collected items are recycled, donated, or repurposed. They partner with local recycling centers and charities to divert waste from landfills. However, the exact percentage can vary by region.

Customer Experience Highlights

  • Friendly crews that often wear branded shirts and arrive on time.
  • Simple online booking with a live‑chat estimate tool.
  • A “no‑surprise” guarantee—what you’re quoted is what you pay.

How 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? Stacks Up

The 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? Model

Founded in 2004, 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? has built a brand around convenience. Their process is similar: you book online, a truck rolls up, and a team loads your junk. The big difference is the pricing structure. Instead of volume, they provide a flat‑rate quote based on the items you list.

Pricing Details

Typical prices start around $150 for a standard residential cleanout. The quote includes labor, disposal, and a recycling fee. Small loads (like a single couch or a few boxes) can feel pricey, but the all‑inclusive nature means you won’t get surprise charges for stairs, heavy objects, or distance.

Coverage and Availability

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? operates in all 50 states, plus Canada. Their extensive network guarantees a same‑day or next‑day pickup in most urban areas. If you live in a remote town, they still service you, though scheduling may require a longer lead time.

Eco‑Friendly Commitment

The company recycles up to 75% of the junk it collects. They also run a “Donate Your Junk” program that partners with local charities—items in good condition are delivered directly to shelters or schools.

Customer Satisfaction Scores

On Trustpilot and Google, 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? averages 4.7/5 stars, thanks to its consistent professionalism and transparent pricing. Reviewers frequently praise the punctuality of crews and the “no‑hassle” disposal process.

Key Comparison Points

Pricing: Volume vs. Flat Rate

For a small job (e.g., a single mattress and a few boxes), Junk King’s per‑yard rate can be cheaper—often under $100. However, if you’re only getting rid of a few items, 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK?’s flat fee may feel higher but includes everything.

For large projects (whole‑house decluttering or remodel debris), Junk King’s volume pricing shines. A three‑yard load can cost under $300, whereas 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK?’s flat‑rate estimate could climb to $400‑$500 depending on the region.

Eco‑Friendly Practices

Both brands recycle heavily, but the nuance lies in transparency. 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? publishes detailed recycling statistics on its website, while Junk King offers a general “up to 80%” claim without a breakdown. If you care deeply about exact numbers, the former may give you more peace of mind.

Service Area and Availability

If you live in a major metro area, you’ll likely get faster service from 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? because of its nationwide footprint. In contrast, Junk King may need a day or two for less‑covered regions, though they do compensate with lower prices.
